#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The agent's test loop (DESIGN.md §15): build, start the whole app, run ONLY the specs currently
# present in e2e/specs (the agent sees only its own checkpoint's spec — blind), then stop.
# PINNED — do not edit. Contract: BASE_CHECKLIST.md §C, §D.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL.
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done

# Install deps + the Chromium browser (both cached after first run), then run the specs.
( cd e2e && npm ci --silent && npx --yes playwright install chromium && npx playwright test )

I've written the acceptance tests. Here's a summary.

## What I did

I added one new spec file, `e2e/specs/client-split-payment.spec.ts`, covering the change request: *"split one lump sum across several invoices; each invoice's balance should come out right."* I did not modify any application source or existing spec — no existing test asserts behaviour this change revises (the invoice-level payment form, statement, and due figures are all unchanged by a new client-level split surface).

## Key findings from exploring first

- **Audit format confirmed empirically.** `PAYMENT_RECORDED id=<invoiceId> amount=<amount>.00` — the `id` is the **invoice** id, not the payment id. (Some existing specs assert the payment id and actually fail at baseline — this checkpoint's spec suite is idealized, with several "existing" specs already red.
